purpose: Intercept the ball before it bounces near the net with a short, compact, firm punch, stepping into the ball with a stable body so the ball is directed with control and depth, then recover ready for the next ball.

phases.description: Ready position at the net: knees slightly bent, racket in front of the body, elbows in front, weight on the balls of the feet.
Split step then a small shoulder turn with a short racket take-back, stepping toward the ball with the opposite foot.
Short forward punch of the firm arm into the ball; contact is out in front of the body at the end of this phase.
Short follow-through, then the arm returns in front and the feet reset to the ready position.

objectives.goal: Keep the take-back short so the racket hand stays in front of the body instead of swinging behind it.

below.looks_like: Racket hand pulled back close to or behind the shoulder in a long groundstroke-style backswing, making timing late and contact soft.

objectives.cue_intent: Remind the player to keep the racket in front and the take-back short, almost no backswing.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels they are swinging the racket back behind them before hitting.
objectives.fix_intent: Have the player shorten the take-back so the hand stays in view, and practise by turning the shoulders rather than swinging the arm back.

objectives.goal: Turn the shoulders slightly toward the ball side as the take-back, rather than hitting with the arm alone.

below.looks_like: Chest stays square to the net, arm-only volley with a hand-reaching, cramped motion.

above.looks_like: Over-rotation of the shoulders, as if for a groundstroke, which makes the punch wide and late.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue a small shoulder turn so the chest points slightly to the side as the ball approaches.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player turns the shoulders or just moves the arm.
objectives.fix_intent: Use a shadow drill: turn the shoulders to put the racket in the take-back position, then punch.

objectives.goal: Bend the knees and stay low and balanced before the punch, getting down to the ball instead of reaching with the arm.

above.looks_like: Standing tall with straight legs, forcing the arm and back to reach for low balls.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to bend the knees and get the body down to the ball.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels stiff-legged or bending down for low balls.
objectives.fix_intent: Practise split step then a lunge-and-bend to low volleys, keeping the head level.

objectives.goal: Step forward into the ball with the body moving toward the net so the contact is made with forward momentum.

below.looks_like: Weight stays back or the player leans away, so the ball is hit late and without depth.

above.looks_like: Lunging or falling forward past the base, losing balance and recovery.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to step toward the ball with the opposite foot and move the weight forward.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels they step forward or stay planted when hitting.
objectives.fix_intent: Drill a step-and-punch with the opposite foot landing as contact is made.

objectives.goal: Meet the ball out in front with a firm, moderately bent elbow, punching without fully straightening or collapsing the arm.

below.looks_like: Elbow stays tightly bent, with the hand close to the body so the ball is jammed and contact is late.

above.looks_like: Arm fully straightened, reaching, reducing control and the ability to adjust.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue a firm arm and punch out in front, with the elbow slightly bent at contact.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels the ball is hitting near the body or at full stretch.
objectives.fix_intent: Use catch-and-punch drills to find contact in front of the body with the elbow slightly bent.

objectives.goal: Make contact well in front of the body with the hand out away from the shoulder.

below.looks_like: Contact beside or behind the body, jammed and late, weak block.

above.looks_like: Overextended reach at maximum stretch, losing control.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to meet the ball out in front of the body.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the ball is reaching the player before they hit it.
objectives.fix_intent: Have the player begin the punch earlier and shift their body toward the ball to find contact out in front.

objectives.goal: Keep a stable, moderately wide base so the body does not wobble during the punch.

below.looks_like: Feet close together, narrow base, easily knocked off balance.

above.looks_like: Overly wide stance, restricting movement and recovery.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to keep a balanced base with the feet about shoulder width apart.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels off balance after the volley.
objectives.fix_intent: Practise a split step to land in a balanced base before every volley.

outcomes.description: The ball is blocked back solidly with control, going over the net and into the court.
The volley lands deep or in a chosen part of the opponent's court.
The volley is compact and balanced in form.

links.mechanism: A short take-back keeps the racket in front so timing and contact stay consistent.
Weight moving forward into the ball gives depth with a short punch, while excessive lunging costs balance.
Contact in front of the body lets the firm arm block the ball without being jammed or overstretched.
Getting low with the legs lets the racket meet low balls with the arm still in front and the head steady.

session_ideas: Shadow volleys: split step, turn, short punch, recover, with the camera side-on.
Partner feeds easy balls to the forehand volley, then the backhand volley, from close range.
Wall volley drill standing about 3 metres away, keeping the racket in front.
Low-volley lunges: step and bend to balls fed at knee height.
Volley-to-volley rally from the service line, focusing on a short take-back.

vocabulary_proposals.name: racket_head
vocabulary_proposals.why: Racket-head position and the angle of the racket face are central to a volley's control (open face for backspin, racket head above the wrist) but cannot be seen from the body features.

vocabulary_proposals.name: contact_point_forward_of_body
vocabulary_proposals.why: Distance of the hand ahead of the front hip or shoulder line at contact would test 'contact in front' more directly than wrist reach from the shoulder.

vocabulary_proposals.name: feet_off_ground (split step)
vocabulary_proposals.why: The split step before the volley could be tested by both heels or ankles leaving the ground; the registered heel features track each foot separately.

vocabulary_proposals.name: ball
vocabulary_proposals.why: Ball position and flight are needed to judge the outcome (depth, placement) and the timing of the split step.

vocabulary_proposals.name: angle.wrist_lay
vocabulary_proposals.why: Wrist firmness (no wrist flick) is a coaching point on volleys, but needs a wrist/hand angle.
